execution_traces.path_summary: Called with LS-RECOVERY-REQUEST. LS-FUNCTION selects one of three phases: INIT opens the two indexed files and validates/sets the recovery mode; RECV recovers a single process ('P'), all processes for a date ('S') or all processes ('A') by reading the batch control record, reading the process definition and restarting, bypassing or terminating the process via REWRITE; TERM issues a completion message through ERRPROC and closes the files. Any other function is reported through 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE. LS-RETURN-CODE is returned in RETURN-CODE and the program GOBACKs.

when_clauses.note: three stacked WHEN phrases share one body (CONTINUE)

Inside the sequential READ NEXT browse loops, 2100-RECOVER-PROCESS issues a keyed READ and a REWRITE on the same BATCH-CONTROL-FILE, which also update WS-BCT-STATUS; effect on browse position and loop termination needs SME review

program_narrative: RCVPRC00 is a batch process-recovery subprogram called with a recovery request (function, process date, process ID, recovery type, return code). An INIT call opens the indexed batch control file (I-O) and the process sequence file (input), checks that a process date and a valid recovery type (P, S or A) are supplied, and records the recovery mode. A RECV call then recovers one process (P), every process for the requested date (S) or every process on file (A): for each process it reads the batch control record and the process definition, and either restarts it (status Ready, restart count incremented, attempt timestamp set) when the definition is restartable, terminates it (status Error, error return code) when the restart count already exceeds the maximum of 3, or bypasses it (status Done, warning return code), rewriting the control record each time. A TERM call reports 'Recovery completed successfully' or 'Recovery completed with errors' through ERRPROC and closes both files. File-status failures, missing records and invalid requests are reported through 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE, which sets the error return code and calls ERRPROC but lets processing continue. The return code is passed back in RETURN-CODE.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
pseudocode: -- Main control: dispatch on the requested function (LS-FUNCTION)
SET RETURN-CODE = ls_return_code  -- pass the result back to the caller / job step
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
IF function = 'INIT' THEN
  CALL 1000-initialize-recovery
ELSE IF function = 'RECV' THEN
  CALL 2000-process-recovery
ELSE IF function = 'TERM' THEN
  CALL 3000-terminate-recovery
ELSE
  SET error_text = 'Invalid function code'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
SET RETURN-CODE = ls_return_code
RETURN to caller

annotations.note: RETURN-CODE is the COBOL special register returned to the caller; not a data item

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-RECOVERY
pseudocode: SELECT CASE recovery_mode  -- WS-RECOVERY-MODE (set during the INIT call)
WHEN 'S':  -- recover all processes for the process date
-- no WHEN OTHER: any other mode does nothing
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SELECT CASE recovery_mode
  WHEN 'P':
    CALL 2100-recover-process
  WHEN 'S':
    CALL 2200-recover-sequence
  WHEN 'A':
    CALL 2300-recover-all
END SELECT

paragraphs.name: 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
pseudocode: -- Common error handler: record the program name and error return code, then log the error
PASSING: error_message  -- ERR-MESSAGE record (ERRHAND copybook) with error_text set by the caller paragraph
-- control returns to the performing paragraph; processing is not stopped
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET error_program = 'RCVPRC00'
SET ls_return_code = BCT-RC-ERROR
CALL program ERRPROC PASSING: error_message

annotations.note: Static CALL to common error-processing subprogram ERRPROC

paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-FILES
pseudocode: OPEN BATCH-CONTROL-FILE for READ-WRITE  -- indexed file BCHCTL, dynamic access, key BCT-KEY
OPEN PROCESS-SEQ-FILE for READ-ONLY  -- indexed file PRCSEQ, dynamic access, key PSR-KEY
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
OPEN BATCH-CONTROL-FILE for READ-WRITE
IF batch_control_file_status != '00' THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error opening control file'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
OPEN PROCESS-SEQ-FILE for READ-ONLY
IF process_seq_file_status != '00' THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error opening sequence file'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

paragraphs.name: 1200-VALIDATE-REQUEST
pseudocode: IF process_date = SPACES THEN  -- LS-PROCESS-DATE not supplied
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
IF process_date = SPACES THEN
  SET error_text = 'Process date required'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
SELECT CASE recovery_type
  WHEN 'P', 'S', 'A':
    -- CONTINUE
  ELSE:
    SET error_text = 'Invalid recovery type'
    CALL 9000-error-routine
END SELECT

paragraphs.name: 1300-SET-RECOVERY-MODE
pseudocode: IF recovery_mode = 'P' AND process_id = SPACES THEN  -- WS-RECOVER-PROCESS; single-process recovery needs a process ID
SET error_text = 'Process ID required for process recovery'
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET recovery_mode = recovery_type
IF recovery_mode = 'P' AND process_id = SPACES THEN
  SET error_text = 'Process ID required for process recovery'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

paragraphs.name: 2100-RECOVER-PROCESS
pseudocode: -- Recover one process identified by process_id and process_date
SET control_job_name = process_id  -- BCT-JOB-NAME (part of BCT-KEY)
SET control_process_date = process_date  -- BCT-PROCESS-DATE (part of BCT-KEY)
READ record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE where key = BCT-KEY
IF record not found THEN  -- INVALID KEY
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET control_job_name = process_id
SET control_process_date = process_date
READ record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE where key = BCT-KEY
IF record not found THEN
  SET error_text = 'Process record not found'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
CALL 2110-determine-action
CALL 2120-execute-recovery

annotations.note: Keyed READ: BCT-KEY also contains BCT-SEQUENCE-NO, which this paragraph does not set
2110/2120 run even if the READ failed, because 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE returns

paragraphs.name: 2110-DETERMINE-ACTION
pseudocode: -- Decide whether to restart, bypass or terminate the process
SET process_seq_process_id = process_id  -- PSR-PROCESS-ID (part of PSR-KEY)
READ record from PROCESS-SEQ-FILE where key = PSR-KEY
IF record not found THEN  -- INVALID KEY
IF process is restartable THEN  -- PSR-RESTARTABLE: PSR-RESTART = 'Y'
SET recovery_action = 'R'  -- SET WS-ACTION-RESTART TO TRUE
IF restart_count > max_restarts THEN  -- BCT-RESTART-COUNT > BCT-MAX-RESTARTS (constant 3)
SET recovery_action = 'T'  -- SET WS-ACTION-TERMINATE TO TRUE
SET recovery_action = 'B'  -- SET WS-ACTION-BYPASS TO TRUE
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET process_seq_process_id = process_id
READ record from PROCESS-SEQ-FILE where key = PSR-KEY
IF record not found THEN
  SET error_text = 'Process definition not found'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
IF process is restartable THEN
  SET recovery_action = 'R'
ELSE
  IF restart_count > max_restarts THEN
    SET recovery_action = 'T'
  ELSE
    SET recovery_action = 'B'
  END IF
END IF

annotations.note: Keyed READ: PSR-KEY also contains PSR-VERSION, which this paragraph does not set

paragraphs.name: 2120-EXECUTE-RECOVERY
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
IF recovery_action = 'R' THEN
  CALL 2121-restart-process
ELSE IF recovery_action = 'B' THEN
  CALL 2122-bypass-process
ELSE IF recovery_action = 'T' THEN
  CALL 2123-terminate-process
END IF

paragraphs.name: 2121-RESTART-PROCESS
pseudocode: -- Mark the process ready to run again
SET current_time = system date-time  -- ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIME FROM TIME STAMP  !! REVIEW: non-standard ACCEPT source
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE  -- REWRITE
IF rewrite failed THEN  -- INVALID KEY
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET control_status = BCT-STAT-READY
INCREMENT restart_count BY 1
SET current_time = system date-time  !! REVIEW
SET attempt_timestamp = current_time
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE
IF rewrite failed THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error updating control record'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

annotations.note: ACCEPT ... FROM TIME STAMP is recorded verbatim; the standard ACCEPT sources are DATE, DAY, DAY-OF-WEEK and TIME

paragraphs.name: 2122-BYPASS-PROCESS
pseudocode: -- Skip the process: mark it done with a warning return code
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE  -- REWRITE
IF rewrite failed THEN  -- INVALID KEY
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET control_status = BCT-STAT-DONE
SET control_return_code = BCT-RC-WARNING
SET control_error_desc = 'Process bypassed by recovery'
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE
IF rewrite failed THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error updating control record'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

paragraphs.name: 2123-TERMINATE-PROCESS
pseudocode: -- Stop the process: mark it in error with an error return code
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE  -- REWRITE
IF rewrite failed THEN  -- INVALID KEY
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET control_status = BCT-STAT-ERROR
SET control_return_code = BCT-RC-ERROR
SET control_error_desc = 'Process terminated by recovery'
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE
IF rewrite failed THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error updating control record'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

paragraphs.name: 2200-RECOVER-SEQUENCE
pseudocode: -- Recover every process recorded for the requested process date
SET control_job_name = MIN_VALUE  -- MOVE LOW-VALUES: lowest job name
POSITION BATCH-CONTROL-FILE at first record with key > BCT-KEY  -- START
IF no such record THEN  -- INVALID KEY
SET error_text = 'No processes found for date'
WHILE batch_control_file_status != '10' DO  -- PERFORM UNTIL WS-BCT-STATUS = '10' (tested before each pass)
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET control_process_date = process_date
SET control_job_name = MIN_VALUE
POSITION BATCH-CONTROL-FILE at first record with key > BCT-KEY
IF no such record THEN
  SET error_text = 'No processes found for date'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
WHILE batch_control_file_status != '10' DO
  READ next record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE
  IF end of file THEN
    SET batch_control_file_status = '10'
  ELSE
    IF control_process_date = process_date THEN
      CALL 2100-recover-process
    END IF
  END IF
END WHILE

annotations.note: Inline PERFORM UNTIL loop; terminates when AT END sets WS-BCT-STATUS to '10' (FILE_EXHAUSTION_LOOP)
2100-RECOVER-PROCESS re-reads and rewrites BATCH-CONTROL-FILE by key inside the sequential browse; SME to confirm browse positioning

paragraphs.name: 2300-RECOVER-ALL
pseudocode: -- Recover every process on the batch control file
SET control_key = MIN_VALUE  -- MOVE LOW-VALUES TO BCT-KEY: start of file
POSITION BATCH-CONTROL-FILE at first record with key > BCT-KEY  -- START
IF no such record THEN  -- INVALID KEY
WHILE batch_control_file_status != '10' DO  -- PERFORM UNTIL WS-BCT-STATUS = '10' (tested before each pass)
SET process_id = control_job_name  -- overwrites the caller's LS-PROCESS-ID
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET control_key = MIN_VALUE
POSITION BATCH-CONTROL-FILE at first record with key > BCT-KEY
IF no such record THEN
  SET error_text = 'No processes found'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
WHILE batch_control_file_status != '10' DO
  READ next record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE
  IF end of file THEN
    SET batch_control_file_status = '10'
  ELSE
    SET process_id = control_job_name
    CALL 2100-recover-process
  END IF
END WHILE

annotations.note: Inline PERFORM UNTIL loop; terminates when AT END sets WS-BCT-STATUS to '10' (FILE_EXHAUSTION_LOOP)
2100-RECOVER-PROCESS then moves LS-PROCESS-DATE (the caller's date, not the record's date) into BCT-PROCESS-DATE before its keyed READ

paragraphs.name: 3100-UPDATE-FINAL-STATUS
pseudocode: PASSING: error_message  -- completion message is logged through the error processor
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
IF ls_return_code = 0 THEN
  SET error_text = 'Recovery completed successfully'
ELSE
  SET error_text = 'Recovery completed with errors'
END IF
CALL program ERRPROC PASSING: error_message

paragraphs.name: 3200-CLOSE-FILES
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
CLOSE BATCH-CONTROL-FILE, PROCESS-SEQ-FILE
IF batch_control_file_status != '00' OR process_seq_file_status != '00' THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error closing files'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
